chapter: San Francisco and the postwar slump
title: Trip to San Francisco and the Backstage
summary: Band change with Tom Archia, a Backstage engagement opposite Scatman Crothers, and Navy players Bennie Green, Jerome Richardson and Grover Mitchell.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Oh yeah, before I get too far, I'd like to mention our trip to San Francisco. We had made one change in the band. J.D. King had left the band, and Tom Archia, a very fine tenor saxophonist, had joined us. For the trip to San Francisco we had... Bill Jones was still singing, with Tom Archia on tenor, Roy Porter on the drums, Bob Kesterson on bass, and Vernon Biddle playing the piano -- he was a very fine pianist.

And we played the Backstage in San Francisco. And it was a really nice place, with a high-rise stage. And again, Scatman Crothers was opposite of us, hah-hah, with his band. That's where I first met Bennie Green, the trombonist. He was in the Navy up there. And Jerome Richardson was in the Navy; I first met him...

Right. Up there at Treasure Island, I think it was. And the trombone player, Grover... Grover Mitchell, yeah. He was in the Navy. In fact, I think we were the first Bebop band they had ever heard! [LAUGHS]
